title: Computing with light
summary: Interferometers steer light to do matrix math; optics also carry data between chips.

links.why: co-packaged optics move into the package

ideas.how: light can move data with less energy, but lasers and converters eat into the savings
interfering light does a matrix multiply

measures.how: optical links aim to lower it between chips

then: Optical fiber carries long-distance data; computing stays electronic.
Optics link servers; silicon photonics moves into data centers.
Optics move into chip packages, and the first photonic processors reach supercomputing centers.
Projection: optical links between chips become standard; photonic compute must prove itself beyond niches.

challenges.task: Set an interferometer's phases to route light or split it in any ratio.
